block.goal: Reduce Expression's FAN-OUT by removing direct dependencies on several specific expression types by extracting their type-casting / type-checking related methods into a new helper class. Net reduction: 3 dependencies (4 removed, 1 added for the new helper).

ops.details: Add imports required by the new helper class that will contain moved methods (static f, Generated, Optional, Consumer).

Extract the type-casting / type-checking methods for these expression types from Expression into a new class ExpressionTypeChecks located in the same package. Move the following groups (each group is all methods referring to the specific expression type):
- AnnotationExpr group: isAnnotationExpr(), asAnnotationExpr(), toAnnotationExpr(), ifAnnotationExpr(Consumer<AnnotationExpr>)
- ArrayAccessExpr group: isArrayAccessExpr(), asArrayAccessExpr(), toArrayAccessExpr(), ifArrayAccessExpr(Consumer<ArrayAccessExpr>)
- ArrayCreationExpr group: isArrayCreationExpr(), asArrayCreationExpr(), toArrayCreationExpr(), ifArrayCreationExpr(Consumer<ArrayCreationExpr>)
- ArrayInitializerExpr group: isArrayInitializerExpr(), asArrayInitializerExpr(), toArrayInitializerExpr(), ifArrayInitializerExpr(Consumer<ArrayInitializerExpr>)
These methods reference their respective expression types (AnnotationExpr, ArrayAccessExpr, ArrayCreationExpr, ArrayInitializerExpr). After extraction, these specific expression-type classes will no longer be referenced directly from Expression; callers internal to the package will be updated to use the new helper.

Update internal references and any internal uses inside Expression to delegate to ExpressionTypeChecks. For example, Expression.isAnnotationExpr() calls (or its callers) should be updated to use ExpressionTypeChecks.isAnnotationExpr(this) or Expression.getTypeChecks().isAnnotationExpr(this). Ensure Expression exposes (or constructs internally) an instance of ExpressionTypeChecks if needed. The intent is that Expression no longer directly contains or references the moved methods' expression-type classes in its own source.
